outcome: Showcase curation rules now have real behaviour tests
owner_impact: Nothing changes in the Showcase: same buttons, same labels, same messages. Its curation rules now live in one small module with 10 tests that check what happens instead of searching the code for exact lines. The rules covered: only a Professor may curate; when the promote button shows 'Promote to Showcase', 'Publish current revision', 'In Showcase' or a save conflict; saving before publishing; placing entries in collections with Uncategorized first; and how an open Showcase entry labels itself read-only. Test now: optional quick look. Sign in as Professor, open one of your Experiments and check the promote button, then open Manage Showcase. Everything should look and behave as before.

next.text: Next is #554: splitting the Experiment registry module (the largest file, the signed-in workspace) into smaller tested parts, starting with a written plan. #554 has not started and waits for the owner's go-ahead.

technical_evidence: New web/src/showcase/curation.js (pure): Professor check, promote-button state, promotion readiness, entry matching, collection choices and labels, confirmations and messages, open-entry labels.
showcase.js delegates those decisions (-99/+76 lines), texts unchanged; an unused helper (hasUnsavedPrivateEdits) removed.
New web/tests/showcase-curation.test.mjs: 10 behaviour tests; three planted rule changes (anyone may curate, 'In Showcase' ignoring unsaved edits, a catalog entry promotable twice) are each caught.
Retired only the 11 source-text assertions (7 test files) whose behaviour the new tests cover, replaced by checks that showcase.js uses the rules; 619 tests pass.
Style comparison of the built Lab identical to the current production build at all four viewports.
